title: Three Seasons and One Short Net
subtitle: 交通出行 · 主题语境阅读
theme: 交通出行（人与自我·生活与学习·出行与交通）
meta: 主题语境：交通出行（人与自我·生活与学习·出行与交通）　|　核心词汇：port　|　正文 344 words　|　高三一轮复习
intro: 请阅读文章，根据上下文判断每一处 port 的含义，再完成 Task 1—Task 3。
passage: In 1993 the fisherman ① entered the port that no boatman in the harbour would have counted, and he said the entering was the whole of the season. The ② port, meaning the harbour itself and not the net, ran three seasons and stayed uncounted in the book; a port, he said, is the only thing in a harbour that is judged by how long it is left uncounted.

Every ③ port in that harbour had the same short net beside it, and the ④ port at the far pier, meaning the catch they kept for the children to land and not either of those, was the only one anybody ever thanked twice. A port, my mother said, is nine parts patience and one part somebody willing to count; the fisherman said the counting is the part that fills three seasons.

My uncle meant the other thing entirely: he said ⑤ the port was the whole of the matter, meaning the trade and not the harbour. The ⑥ port, meaning the trade and not any of that, is the only thing in a matter that everybody waits for and nobody counts; port, he said, is either something you enter or the only word that means both a harbour and a trade. He said the trade is the part they remember.

By 1998 the ⑦ port had become a line in a logbook, and the logbook had become an argument about the short net. The ⑧ port of the whole thing, the fisherman wrote in July, was one harbour and three seasons of counting; port, he said, is either the catch at the far pier or the reason you learned to count. He said the counting was never mentioned.

The ⑨ port I remember is the harbour counted in the logbook, which closed in 2000 and is still counted as the quietest in the harbour. A ⑩ port, my mother said in 2002, is the only harbour that improves by being counted; every port, she said, is a trade that has agreed to look like a harbour. She said the trade was the honest half.

task1.title: Task 1　语境辨义
task1.intro: 请将对应义项填入表中。
options: A. n. 港口（指渔港里每一座旁边的那一座）
B. n. 港口（指那座港口本身，与小小的渔网相对）
C. 固定搭配：enter the port 进这一座港口
D. n. 港口（指留给孩子们起的那一网）
E. n. 港口之事（抽象总称，指一处渔港的港口之事）
F. n. 港口（指航海日志里写到、被清点的那一座）
G. n. 港口、门路（指一件事里人人都捕却无人提起的那样东西）
H. n. 门路（抽象总称，指人人都捕却无人提起的那样东西）

items.q: entered the port that no boatman in the harbour would have counted
The port, meaning the harbour itself and not the net
the port at the far pier
the port was the whole of the matter
the port had become a line in a logbook
The port of the whole thing
A port, my mother said in 2002

answers.why: enter the port 意为“进这一座港口”，1993 年那位渔人把渔港里没有一位船工肯清点的一座港口做了一遍。
port 意为“港口”，指那座港口本身而不是小小的渔网，它经过了三个汛期而在簿子上没有被清点。
port 意为“港口”，指渔港里每一座旁边的那一座，每一座旁边都有同一张小小的渔网。
port 意为“港口”，指最远那座码头的留给孩子们起的那一网，是唯一有人谢过两次的。
port 意为“港口、门路”，指一件事里人人都捕却无人提起的那样东西，叔叔说这座门路就是那件事的全部。
port 意为“门路”，指人人都捕却无人提起的那样东西而不是那座港口，是事情里人人都等、却无人说破的东西。
port 意为“港口”，指航海日志里写到、被清点的那一座，到 1998 年这一座成了航海日志里的一行。
port 意为“港口之事”，渔人七月写道，整件事的港口之事是一处渔港和三个汛期的清点。
port 意为“港口”，我记得的是航海日志里清点过的那一座，2000 年归港了，至今仍被说成渔港里最安静的一座。
port 为抽象总称，母亲 2002 年说，港口是唯一会因为被好好清点而变得更好的港口。
